notes: M1 schema window. Every release widens the window, never narrows it inside an expand window: the previous binary must remain usable until the matching contract step has shipped and been observed in the field. Widened to 22 by 0022_observation_hosted_attribution.expand.sql, which is expand-only: it drops a NOT NULL and adds columns and a CHECK, so a binary that predates it reads a database with an extra nullable column and ignores it, which is the direction that window exists to permit. Widened to 23 by 0023_site_isolation_for_every_site_bearing_table.expand.sql, which adds NO column and NO data and only creates policies, so a binary that predates it operates on a database with more predicates than it expects and the difference is entirely in whether a cross-site statement is refused. That is the safe direction for an old binary and is why this migration is expand-only: the row shapes are identical, so a 22-era binary keeps working against a 23 database and simply sees the policies its own code already relied on. Widened to 24 by 0024_search_documents.expand.sql, which adds a GENERATED STORED column and a GIN index over it and creates a view. A binary that predates it reads a database with an extra column it never names, so the column is invisible to it, and with one more index the planner may use for a query it does not issue. No row shape changes, which is why this is an expand rather than a contract step. Widened to 25 by 0025_future_partitions.expand.sql, which adds monthly partitions for 2028-2030 to inbox_events and canonical_events and applies RLS policies. A binary that predates it reads a database with more partitions it never names, so the partitions are invisible to it, and the DEFAULT partitions already present ensure the old binary keeps accepting writes. No row shape changes, which is why this is an expand step.
